Whole-lake C, N and P fluxes from the GLM-AED diagnostic output

Source: R/glm_fluxes.R
calc_glm_fluxes.Rd

Integrates the diagnostic variables that libaed-water writes to the GLM output.nc (process rates per m3, and fluxes across the sediment-water and air-water interfaces per m2) over the lake, giving mmol per day for each process. This is the basis of the budget returned by diag_glm_budget() and drawn by plot_glm_budget(): it shows where each element comes from and goes to, and so where a concentration that is out of balance is being made or lost.

Usage

calc_glm_fluxes(
  aeme = NULL,
  file = NULL,
  element = c("N", "P", "C"),
  path = NULL,
  settling = c("hypsograph", "interface")
)

Arguments

aeme

Aeme object that has been run with glm_aed. Not needed if file is given.

file

character; path to the GLM output.nc. If NULL it is found from aeme.

element

character; any of "C", "N" and "P".

path

character; root directory used with aeme.

settling

character; how settling to the sediment is calculated, "hypsograph" (default) or "interface". See Details.

Value

a tibble with columns Date, element, process, from, to, var (the netCDF variable) and value (mmol/d, daily mean). The attribute missing lists the flux patterns for which GLM wrote no variable.

Details

Volumetric rates (mmol/m3/d) are multiplied by the layer volumes, sediment zone fluxes (*_Z, mmol/m2/d) by zarea and surface fluxes by surface_area. Each flux is positive in the direction from to to (see the from and to columns), so the sediment-water exchange sediment to pom is negative when particles are settling out.

Only variables that GLM wrote are used. AED writes most fluxes only when the module diag_level is high enough (diag_level = 10 gives everything; the *_swi terms need at least 2) and the _Z zone variables need sediment zones, so a run with fewer diagnostics gives a less complete picture. The variables that were looked for but not found are listed in the missing attribute of the result.

Denitrification is the sum of NIT_denit and, when the organic matter module is coupled to nitrate (simDenitrification), OGM_doc_denit, which holds nitrogen despite its carbon label.

Settling to the sediment is worked out from the per-layer settling rates (OGM_pon_set, PHY_<group>_set_n, ...) and the hypsograph: sum(rate * layer thickness * (A[k] - A[k - 1])), where the area change across a layer is the sediment that particles settling through it can land on. The sediment-water interface diagnostics (OGM_pon_swi_Z, PHY_phy_swi_*) report the same thing but in the lake tested here were 10 to 30 times larger than vvel * concentration allows (AED scales the layer rate by a thickness that is not that of the layer), and the water column inventory only closes with the hypsograph-based value. Use settling = "interface" to see the interface values instead.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
fx <- calc_glm_fluxes(aeme, element = "N")
dplyr::summarise(fx, mean = mean(value), .by = c(process, from, to))
} # }
